metadata.title: Success of ChatGPT, an AI language model, in taking the French language version of the European Board of Ophthalmology examination: A novel approach to medical knowledge assessment.

abstract:
PURPOSE
The purpose of this study was to evaluate the performance of ChatGPT, a cutting-edge artificial intelligence (AI) language model developed by OpenAI, in successfully completing the French language version of the European Board of Ophthalmology (EBO) examination and to assess its potential role in medical education and knowledge assessment.


METHODS
ChatGPT, based on the GPT-4 architecture, was exposed to a series of EBO examination questions in French, covering various aspects of ophthalmology. The AI's performance was evaluated by comparing its responses with the correct answers provided by ophthalmology experts. Additionally, the study assessed the time taken by ChatGPT to answer each question as a measure of efficiency.


RESULTS
ChatGPT achieved a 91% success rate on the EBO examination, demonstrating a high level of competency in ophthalmology knowledge and application. The AI provided correct answers across all question categories, indicating a strong understanding of basic sciences, clinical knowledge, and clinical management. The AI model also answered the questions rapidly, taking only a fraction of the time needed by human test-takers.


CONCLUSION
ChatGPT's performance on the French language version of the EBO examination demonstrates its potential to be a valuable tool in medical education and knowledge assessment. Further research is needed to explore optimal ways to implement AI language models in medical education and to address the associated ethical and practical concerns.

Résumé Objectif L’objectif de cette étude était d’évaluer la performance de ChatGPT, un modèle de langage d’intelligence artificielle (IA) développée par OpenAI, dans la réussite des annales françaises de l’examen de l’European Board of Ophthalmology (EBO) et d’évaluer son rôle potentiel dans l’éducation médicale et l’évaluation des connaissances.  Méthodes ChatGPT, basé sur l’architecture GPT-4, a été exposé à une série de questions d’examen de l’EBO en français qui couvraient divers aspects de l’ophtalmologie. La performance de l’IA a été évaluée en comparant ses réponses avec les réponses correctes fournies par des experts en ophtalmologie. En outre, l’étude a évalué le temps pris par ChatGPT pour répondre à chaque question en tant que mesure de l’efficacité.  Résultats ChatGPT a obtenu un taux de réussite de 91 % à l’examen EBO, démontrant un haut niveau de compétence en matière de connaissances et d’applications ophtalmologiques. L’IA a fourni des réponses correctes dans toutes les catégories de questions, ce qui indique une bonne compréhension des sciences fondamentales, des connaissances cliniques et de la gestion clinique. Le modèle d’IA a également répondu rapidement aux questions, ne prenant qu’une fraction du temps nécessaire aux examinateurs humains.  Conclusion La performance de ChatGPT dans l’examen EBO démontre son potentiel en tant qu’outil dans l’éducation médicale et l’évaluation des connaissances. Des recherches supplémentaires sont nécessaires pour explorer les meilleures façons de mettre en œuvre les modèles de langage de l’IA dans l’enseignement médical et pour répondre aux préoccupations éthiques et pratiques qui y sont associées. In recent years, AI has been employed to aid physicians in diagnostics, treatment planning, and research [1] . One of the most remarkable AI technologies is ChatGPT, an advanced language model developed by OpenAI [2] . Upon its release in November 2022, the AI chatbot, ChatGPT, quickly became a hot topic, particularly for its use in the context of education. It rapidly demonstrated its ability to answer exam-style questions [3]  and provide explanations, raising questions about its potential role in education and assessment [4] . Recently, it has been used for writing scientific articles [4]  without being detected by human experts [5] . Thus, it is essential to ascertain the accuracy with which ChatGPT can answer questions on medical examinations. This evaluation may offer insight into the potential use of ChatGPT by medical students in their learning and the most effective ways to integrate it into their educational journey. In this study, we present the results of ChatGPT's performance on the French language version of the European Board of Ophthalmology (EBO) examination, which is a rigorous test assessing the competency of ophthalmologists across Europe [6] .  Materials and methods We designed a comprehensive study to test the AI's performance on the French version of the EBO examination, focusing on knowledge and application of ophthalmic principles and practice. We utilized the latest version of ChatGPT, which is based on the GPT-4 architecture. This model had been trained on extensive data, including medical texts and journals, up to September 2021 [2] . The EBO examination consists of two parts: Part 1, which covers basic sciences and clinical knowledge, and Part 2, which consists of an oral examination focusing on clinical management and decision-making [6] . To review for the EBO, French students use a collection of similar questions and answers in French created by a committee of ophthalmology professors. This collection consists of 1357 tests across all question categories (multiple-choice questions, short answer questions, true and false questions, clinical scenarios, and theoretical questions). Each test has 5 questions to answer. These questions are grouped into 19 modules (Fig. 1  ). In total, 6785 questions were processed by ChatGPT. We adapted the examination format for ChatGPT by providing it with questions from the French examination, ensuring that the AI would not have prior knowledge of the specific questions. An independent operator collected the responses of ChatGPT and scored them against the correct answers provided by the ophthalmology experts. No approval from the institutional review board or informed consent was required for this study.  Results ChatGPT correctly answered 6188 out of 6785 questions. ChatGPT achieved a 91.2% success rate on the French language EBO examination, demonstrating a high level of competency in ophthalmology knowledge and application. The AI excelled across all question categories of the examination, indicating a strong understanding of basic sciences, clinical knowledge, and clinical management. The AI model was also able to answer the questions rapidly, taking only a fraction of the time needed by human being (on the order of one second).  Discussion ChatGPT's ability to succeed on a written examination, as demonstrated by the 91% success rate on the French EBO examination, highlights the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) in medicine. As AI technology continues to advance, its application has expanded into various domains, including medical diagnosis, treatment planning, and medical education [1,7] . ChatGPT, based on the GPT-4 architecture, was trained on an extensive dataset, including medical texts and journals, up until September 2021 [2] . This extensive training will enable ChatGPT to process and understand complex medical information, leading to a high level of competency on written examinations such as that of the EBO. Previous studies have also shown the efficacy of AI-powered tools in medical applications, such as dermatologist-level classification of skin cancer [8] , detection of diabetic retinopathy on retinal fundus photographs [9]  or, more recently, detection of cataract [10,11]  and corneal edema [12]  on OCT scans. It is interesting to note the incorrect responses from ChatGPT in our study. First, ChatGPT was unable to interpret figures, graphs or tables. To avoid biasing the analysis, questions containing these elements were removed from the questionnaire before analysis. Second, ChatGPT was more likely to make errors if the question was ambiguous, poorly worded or contained abbreviations. The AI has difficulties with the notion of “ability” in some situations and with judgmental assessments. In addition, some epidemiological data was unavailable online, and some standards of medical care had recently changed; thus, for certain questions, ChatGPT could not give the correct answer. In fact, ChatGPT's knowledge is based on data available up to September 2021, which means that it may not be aware of recent advances in the medical field. In order to maintain the accuracy and relevance of the AI, it needs to be continuously updated and trained with the latest medical literature [13] . On the other hand, ChatGPT had the ability to select the most appropriate answer, even if it was not the correct answer. In Fig. 2 A , the multiple-choice question has a typographical error, so that there is no correct answer. ChatGPT suggests the answer that is closest to the correct answer and completes its answer with an alternative correct answer (Fig. 2 B). Despite the lack of interpretive capability, the power of the algorithm allows for an improvement in the educational message. In addition, an improvement in version 4 of ChatGPT now allows answers to multiple-choice questions with more than one correct answer, or “best answer” type questions, which previous algorithms could not handle [14] . In January 2023, Sun Huh [14]  compared the knowledge and interpretation skills of ChatGPT with those of medical students in Korea by administering a parasitology exam to both ChatGPT and medical students. It is interesting to note that the performance of ChatGPT was lower than that of the well-trained medical students, and the correct answer rate of ChatGPT was not related to the level of knowledge of the items in question. This result is due to the highly specific nature of the test administered, and we believe that ChatGPT's knowledge and interpretation abilities will rapidly improve through deep learning, similar to the ability of AlphaGo [15] . Therefore, medical/health professors and students should consider how to integrate this AI platform into medical/health education in the near future. Furthermore, AI should be integrated into the curriculum of medical schools, and some schools have already done so [16] . The results of our study indicate the potential for AI, and ChatGPT in particular, to make a positive contribution to medical education and practice. The success of AI on the French EBO examination might pave the way for further integration of AI technology into medical education and continuing professional development [7] . ChatGPT's proficiency in clinical management and decision-making suggests that it could be a valuable resource for practicing ophthalmologists and other medical professionals seeking information and guidance on complex cases [8] . Furthermore, while ChatGPT has demonstrated good results, it is not a replacement for human clinicians. AI technology should be seen as a complement to medical professionals, not a replacement [13] . Collaboration between human expertise and AI-driven tools can lead to improved patient outcomes and more efficient healthcare delivery [17] . The question of the role of AI in education and knowledge assessment is critical. AI models such as ChatGPT might be used as learning assistants, providing personalized feedback and additional explanations to enhance the learning process. ChatGPT might also be used in educational assessments to identify students’ knowledge gaps and provide targeted recommendations for improvement. In addition, AI-powered testing platforms might be developed to provide adaptive examinations that adjust the level of difficulty in real time based on a student's performance. In conclusion, ChatGPT's successful performance on the French language version of the EBO examination demonstrates the potential for AI to positively impact medical education and practice. With a 91% success rate, ChatGPT has shown its potential as a valuable resource for ophthalmologists and other medical professionals seeking guidance on complex cases. However, it is important to recognize that AI technology should be utilized as a supplement to human expertise, not as a replacement. Further research and development of AI-driven tools such as ChatGPT can contribute to the advancement of medical knowledge and the enhancement of patient care. key_findings.claim: ChatGPT (GPT-4) achieved a 91.2% success rate on the French language European Board of Ophthalmology (EBO) examination, correctly answering 6188 out of 6785 questions
key_findings.context: Questions with figures, graphs, or tables were excluded prior to analysis; the examination covered 19 modules and 5 question types

key_findings.claim: ChatGPT performed competently across all EBO question categories including basic sciences, clinical knowledge, and clinical management
key_findings.quantitative_result: Consistent performance across all 19 modules and all question formats
key_findings.context: EBO Part 1 covers basic sciences and clinical knowledge; Part 2 focuses on clinical management

key_findings.claim: ChatGPT answered ophthalmology examination questions in approximately one second, representing a fraction of the time required by human test-takers
key_findings.context: Speed was assessed informally as a secondary measure of efficiency; no formal comparison against human timing was performed

key_findings.claim: ChatGPT was unable to interpret figures, graphs, or tables, requiring exclusion of such questions before analysis
key_findings.context: Questions containing visual elements were systematically removed to avoid biasing the analysis

key_findings.claim: ChatGPT demonstrated the ability to identify the most appropriate answer when a question contained a typographical error rendering the officially correct answer invalid
key_findings.context: Illustrated via a multiple-choice question about corneal wound suture where the correct answer '10-0 nylon monofilament' was misprinted as '0-0 nylon monofilament'; ChatGPT selected the closest correct option and noted the discrepancy

key_findings.claim: ChatGPT was more likely to make errors on ambiguous, poorly worded, or heavily abbreviated questions, and on items requiring interpretation of judgmental or epidemiological data updated after September 2021
key_findings.context: Qualitative analysis of incorrect responses; no quantitative breakdown by error type provided

llm_extraction.methods_summary: ChatGPT (GPT-4 architecture, knowledge cutoff September 2021) was administered the full French-language EBO examination question bank comprising 6785 questions across 1357 tests and 19 ophthalmology modules. Question formats included multiple-choice, short-answer, true/false, clinical scenarios, and theoretical questions. Questions containing figures, graphs, or tables were excluded prior to testing to avoid bias from ChatGPT's inability to process visual content. An independent operator submitted questions to ChatGPT and scored responses against expert-provided correct answers. Response time per question was also recorded informally. No institutional review board approval or informed consent was required.
llm_extraction.limitations: 1. Questions containing figures, graphs, or tables were excluded before analysis, likely inflating the reported success rate relative to the full examination as taken by human candidates. 2. No formal comparison against human test-taker performance on the same question set was performed, preventing assessment of relative competency. 3. ChatGPT's training data has a cutoff of September 2021, so questions requiring knowledge of recent clinical guidelines or epidemiological updates were disadvantaged. 4. The study tested only a single AI model (GPT-4-based ChatGPT) without comparison to other LLMs or earlier ChatGPT versions. 5. No statistical analysis beyond a simple percentage was reported; no confidence intervals, stratified performance by module or question type, or significance tests were provided. 6. The examination questions were developed for French students and may not represent the full range of EBO examination difficulty, potentially overestimating generalizability. 7. The study design does not permit causal inference about what aspects of GPT-4 architecture drive ophthalmology performance.

relationships.description: Panthier & Gatinel extend Huh (2023), who found ChatGPT performance below that of well-trained Korean medical students on a parasitology exam; the current study shows domain and question-set specificity strongly modulates ChatGPT performance, with 91% on a broader ophthalmology bank contrasting with lower scores on a highly specialised parasitology exam

The EBO success rate supports the broader thesis from Esteva et al. (2017) that AI can achieve expert-level or near-expert-level performance on specialised medical knowledge tasks, extending that finding from image-based diagnosis to text-based examination

Findings support the trajectory established by Gulshan et al. (2016) that AI achieves clinically relevant performance thresholds in ophthalmology, here demonstrated in a knowledge-assessment rather than image-classification context

Results corroborate the concern raised by Stokel-Walker (2022) that ChatGPT can successfully complete academic examinations, now demonstrated in a rigorous, expert-validated medical board examination context

methodology_details.approach: Prospective benchmark evaluation of ChatGPT (GPT-4) on the complete French-language EBO examination question bank; independent operator scored AI responses against expert-validated answer keys across all question types and 19 specialty modules
datasets: French EBO examination question bank: 1357 tests, 6785 questions, 19 ophthalmology modules, developed by Collège d'ophtalmologie des universitaires de France (COUF)
methodology_details.reproducibility_notes: Supplementary data file (mmc1.doc) contains the full 6785-question set. No code or prompting protocol was published. Independent operator scoring introduced a single-evaluator dependency; inter-rater reliability not reported.

domain_specific_fields.benchmark: European Board of Ophthalmology (EBO) French-language examination — 6785 questions across 19 modules, 5 question formats
domain_specific_fields.metrics: Success rate 91.2% (6188/6785 correct); response time ~1 second per question
domain_specific_fields.model_architecture: GPT-4 (ChatGPT, OpenAI; training data cutoff September 2021)
domain_specific_fields.dataset: 6785 questions from 1357 French ophthalmology tests across 19 COUF modules; questions with figures/tables excluded prior to analysis
